questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Berlin is a vibrant city full of culture with many theaters and museums. That was partly was drew me to Berlin. I would actually have liked to go to Hamburg og Leipzig, but that was not possible. I choose Berlin because it was what i could get in Germany with my application, bacause I wanted to learn the language, but that is indeed hard in Berlin because its so international.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level of education within the classroom was lower than in Copenhagen and therefore the learning came mostly from the texts and being in another city.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was good, i got the assitence i needed and knew i was always possible to find help somewhere, the international office in Berlin was friendly and helpfull. My girlfriend had just been there so a lot of info i just got from her.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an info meeting where all information was given, it was well structured and you felt safe. What was always a bit of a worry was getting enough ects and because Germany has a system so different from the rest of the world you were always a bit worried. Also as a Dane it can be a bit shocking coming to a world without any digitalization.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Information about how their ects system and exam system is intended to work would have been a gift !

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy. Take all the help you can get. The market is crazy and the people renting out pretty crazy, no one lives in a good flat in Berlin a a student which is in fact quite crazy, the priviledge of a Danish passport are huge! I could say the best way to get housing is trying to find something with other Danes, maybe someone you travel there with. Everyone i knew there lived kind of shir

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The housing market in Berlin is crazy, and you will most likely live with someone quite weird and different from how we live in Denmark, it can be fun but also sometimes quite frustrating. Spending some time and cash finding a good place to stay i key. I lived in Neu-Kölln and the area was lovely, living of campus gives a great feeling of the pulsating and crazy city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When we think about how good the housing for students is in copenhagen it is really bad in Berlin, the dorms where not a place you wanted to live - dirty and with no soul and far away from anything including public transport.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some thing were weird and the system looks old and weird. There is also no info on how to find the course catalogue and once you find it, sometimes all the info is not there, but you learn to navigate in it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I har to apply online, it was pretty forward, but also kind of a lot to fill out

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I dont know if there was any actually

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write exams. It always possible to get more ects, so don't be scared i will be solved

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level as i said is lover than in CPH, but i found the classses nice anyhow and got to learn something i did not expect and got to learn how other cultures look at learning and being a student.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was lower than in Copenhagen. A lot was for me basic and felt useless a times, but there were also good classes and good teachers. The don't really discuss the text and just talk more broadly, the teachers could try to close some discussion laeding nowhere down a little bit sooner

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: KU uses more time on the text and the theory

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sex and Socialism: Gender, sexuality and the boundaries of the nation state in post-war Central and Southeastern Europe
Der Russiche Bürgerkrieg
Der Nahe Osten und Europa im 20. Jahrhundert
Borders and Border Regions in 20th Century Europe
Global History of Capitalism
The End oft the Cold War and the Search for a New World Order in Europe

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hannes Grandits is great and techeas relly good in comparisson to the other teachers. The level in his class was good and he really knows what he is talking about and is well structured.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It is cheap to live in Berlin in comparisson to CPH, but housing is hard to find and usually shitty if you are not from Berlin og have an big network. I don't know if something was unexpected, as i have mentioned earlier my Girlfriend had lived there for 6 months when i got there, so she already had a life for us. When coming to Berlin from DK what you experience is that everything is cheaper and you suddenly feel almost rich ...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food and other convience thing were a lot cheaper. Things like creams and luxury soap was about half the price of in Denmark, chocolate and other sweets are also cheap. Going out to eat is as cheap as cooking at home in Denmark and the nicer restaurants and bars are also a lot cheaper, as i have said, the most is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not take part in any so i dont really have much to say about it ... What i can say is that i would recommend doing it, i know noone from Berlin and spend all my time with people i knew from before ... I you wanna meet people i thinks there are great offers. I would say that an intro to what happened on campus would be nice, what was offered to us was erasmus specific and i would have liked to know what happened for the normal students

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all kinds, i saw sport and clubs for reading.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: depends, I didn't do any so i can't really recommend any - i did some tours with the sprachkurs and they were nice. I got to go in theater and that was a good experience and a good introdution to what exists in the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Leipzig. Is a short trip and its possible to go with the deutschland ticket for free. The city is a nice little breating space with loads of culture and a nice city life. I you have the time i would say that going to potsdam for the art museum there i also a nice thing to do they have a good collection of impresionism

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Copenhageners will find berlin big but the culture is very much the same. Bikes are not the king of the street, the car is. I would say its okay easy to get around the city by bike but most of the time you will need to go by U-bahn and that takes som time getting used to. The culture is very open and everyone is proud of being multicultural and therefore the most locals love expads.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in the classroom and just ask them what they are doing in the weekend, i found that some were a bit tired of all the expads and others just loved meeting new people. Other than that i have no tips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the german past is a tricky subject and their relationship to Israel is also very tricky to talk about. It is something that should be talked about carefully, but most young people can talk about it in a nice way.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: cultural opneness and the cultural life with the many good theaters and the nice museums, that i will miss along with the döner

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: do exams, dont take 30 credits worth of courses, i cant stress this enough. The exams are easy in comparisson to CPH and doing 30 ects of classes i a lot of reading work. Most teachers will ask you to do something to prove you have read so its a lot of work doing the classes. The exams can be an essay or a small discussion of something

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: spend money on the housing, a good place to live with people you like is a perfect way into a good life, i did not do that and regret it totally

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: to live in berlin and experience the art scene. I feel now tha got a place to go once i get to tired of copenhagen and a place to go an experience art as i love a lot and often feel like i dont have time for in copenhagen between work and studies.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing and living with an american and an old hash smoking dude. That was pretty tough and a felt like i was a constant stressed until i rented something with my girlfriend. I also felt lonely a times. In such a big city it is easy to feel alone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I thing a have said anything i can, i would much rather come talk to someone that has to go, i would love to help in any other way than filling something like this out.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
